note: Two bugs caused all three deaths. First, the speed was measured against the drifting clouds, which showed 0.31–0.34 px/ms while the obstacles actually moved about 0.42–0.45 px/ms (dx and gameMs in the logs agree). Because of that, the jump simulation planned a jump that was too short and waited until dx≈15 before jumping. On seeds 101 and 303 the dino cleared the first cactus but landed on the next group 250 px later. Second, a jump or duck key press makes the game redraw only the dino, and the state is read right after the press, so those frames had no ground and no obstacles. On seed 202 the bird disappeared as soon as the dino ducked: the rules released the duck and the dino stood up into the bird. The fixes: (1) speed is now ground scroll per ms of game time, using info.lagMs as the time between frames (falls back to cloud drift at about 12 ms/px when lagMs is 0). (2) Frames drawn without the ground reuse the last obstacles, moved forward by the elapsed time. (3) The jump is simulated in ms: find the safe take-off window, aim for its middle, and pull it earlier when the next obstacle needs room to land and jump again (or pick a single jump that clears both). The rules are unchanged.
instructions:
Apply these rules in order and pick the first that matches.
1. If over is true: choose JUMP (restarts the game).
2. If player.phase is "rising": choose JUMP (keep the key held all the way up; releasing it while rising cuts the jump into a low hop that lands on the cactus).
3. If player.phase is "falling": choose NOOP (release the key so the next jump is a fresh press).
4. If threat is null: choose NOOP.
5. If threat.duckable is true and threat.impactMs <= 250: choose DUCK (keep choosing it until the bird has passed).
6. If threat.jumpTiming is "ok" or "late": if jumpReady is false choose NOOP (release for one decision so the key can be pressed fresh), otherwise choose JUMP.
7. Otherwise (jumpTiming "early" or "n/a"): choose NOOP and wait.
Notes: player.phase is ground / rising / falling. threat is the nearest obstacle that can still hit the dino (high birds, stars and the moon are already left out; on the ground, obstacles already behind the dino are dropped); it stays in place on frames where only the dino was redrawn after a key press. speed is px per ms of game time. dx, impactMs and passMs are measured from the moment the action takes effect. jumpTiming comes from simulating a full jump (about 570 ms) pressed now against the threat and the obstacle after it: "early" means wait (a jump now would land on it, or a later moment is safer, or an earlier one would not leave room to land and jump the next obstacle), "ok" means jump now, "late" means no safe moment is left so jump immediately anyway, and "n/a" means not a jump case (a bird to duck under, or the dino is in the air). jumpReady is false while ducking, and for one decision when the last press did not start a jump.

actions.description: Press ArrowUp to jump from the ground (needs a fresh press); keep it held while rising for a full-height jump; also restarts the game
Duck under mid-height birds (hold while the bird passes)

tests.why: Night-mode stars (9x9 sprites high in the sky) must never show up as obstacles.
A sky decoration must never become the threat that triggers a jump.
The star that caused the mistimed jump before the small cactus must be filtered out.
With only a star and an overhead bird ahead, the dino must stay on the ground instead of jumping into the bird.
When the dino lands before the large cactus, the threat must be the cactus rather than a star, so the jump is timed to the cactus.

v4 divided each decision's scroll by an assumed 30 ms while about 42 ms pass, so it reported 0.5-0.65 px/ms against a true value of about 0.44 and jumped too early. Speed is now ground scroll per game frame (frames counted from clouds, which drift 1 px per frame) divided by 16 ms.
The same speed fix, checked earlier in a game (about 4-7 s), where the ground moves 6-7 px per 16 ms frame.
Right after the fatal take-off (alt 31, then 40), the dino must be read as rising so that the jump key stays held.
The same check for the seed-303 death, where the jump was cut to a 54 px hop and came down on a small cactus.
All three v4 deaths were short hops caused by releasing ArrowUp about 40 ms after the press, just past Chrome's 30 px minimum jump height. The key must stay held while the dino is rising.

Pressing the duck key makes the game redraw only the dino, and that frame was read with no ground and no bird. v5 then dropped the threat and released DUCK, and the dino stood up into the bird. While ducking, the bird must stay the threat (carried over from the last full frame).

Obstacles moved about 0.42-0.45 px per game ms (dx against gameMs), but the cloud-based estimate read 0.31. The jump was therefore planned too short and too late. Speed is now ground scroll over the game time between frames.
The same speed fix, checked on the seed-303 death (about 12 s into the game).
v5 still said early at dx 29 and jumped at dx 15. It cleared the first cactus but landed on the next group 250 px later. With the right speed, a small cactus within 30 px must never be 'wait'.
The same late-jump death on seed 303 (early at dx 24, jumped at dx 11, landed on the following cacti).
